q: On which date Part XVII of the Constitution was passed in Parliament?
e: Option B is correct. Part XVII of the Constitution — the Official Language part (Articles 343–351) — was passed in Parliament on 14 September 1949, a date celebrated every year as Hindi Diwas. q: When was Official Language Act 1963 passed?
e: 10.05.1963 — that is the right answer. . The Official Languages Act, 1963 was passed on 10 May 1963, continuing the use of English for official purposes of the Union beyond 1965 alongside Hindi. It was amended in 1967 to give indefinite continuance to English. Related exam fact: Part XVII of the Constitution was passed on 14 September 1949. A useful way to verify this in the exam hall is to ask what would break if the opposite were true — the logic of the underlying system points straight to this option.

q: When was Official Language Act 1963 amended?
e: Option A (1967) is the correct choice. . The Official Languages Act, 1963 was amended in 1967 — the amendment removed the 15-year sunset on the use of English, allowing English to continue indefinitely alongside Hindi for official purposes of the Union. Related exam fact: sections 6 and 7 of the Act did not apply to Jammu and Kashmir. The principle behind this is worth grasping, not just memorising: once you understand why the rule is framed this way, the answer follows naturally instead of needing rote recall.

q: In which state Sections 6 & 7 of Official Language Act 1963 do not apply?
e: Option A is correct. Sections 6 and 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 — dealing with the authorised Hindi translation of laws and the optional use of Hindi in judgments and decrees of High Courts — did not apply to the State of Jammu and Kashmir. The Official Languages policy promotes progressive use of Hindi in official work, with prescribed targets and inspections.
